about.desc: Bluetooth fingerprint authentication: unlock the screen by fingerprint, dual-host management, OTA firmware update. Screen unlock is built on a Credential Provider.
about.name: About immurok
about.ota.desc: Automatically check for the latest firmware online and update the device over the air. Make sure the device has more than 50% battery remaining before updating.
about.title: About
device.dual.desc: A device can bind up to two hosts. Use the device's switch fingerprint to toggle between them.
device.dual.desc_offline: This host is still bound to a device that is not connected right now. Unbinding here only clears the local binding, so you can pair with a new device.
device.pair.hint: Press the device button to confirm during pairing; if the device is already bound to another host, press an enrolled fingerprint first, then the button.
device.pair.hint.fresh: No host is registered on the device yet — pairing takes one step: press the physical button on the device once to confirm (it blinks white while waiting).
device.pair.need_connect: Device not connected. Pair and connect the immurok device in Windows Bluetooth settings first. If it is currently linked to the other host, disconnect it there or move that host out of range.
device.pair.slot_hint: The device is already bound to another host, so this PC will take slot {0}. Pairing takes two steps: ① press an enrolled fingerprint on the device; ② then press the physical button to confirm.
device.pair.slots_full: Both host slots on the device are taken. Unbind one of them (hover a slot row below) before pairing this PC.
device.pair.stale: The slot this PC occupies on the device (slot {0}) is empty, so the local binding is void — it was most likely unbound from the other host. Pairing again overwrites it.
device.pair.stale_reset: The device no longer holds a binding for this PC (it may have been reset). Pairing again overwrites the stale local binding.
device.subtitle: Connection, pairing & dual-host management
enroll.title: Enroll fingerprint
features.agent.hint: Require a fingerprint before an AI agent runs a command via imk run --agent.
features.lock.hint: Hold your finger on the sensor for ~2s to lock the screen. Off by default.
features.otp.hint: Read TOTP codes from the device, in the client and via imk get.
features.ssh.hint: Sign SSH/git operations with keys held on the device, authorized by fingerprint.
features.subtitle: Turn individual capabilities on or off
features.unlock.hint: Submit your saved password to unlock the lock screen when your fingerprint matches.
features.unlock.nopassword: ⚠ Login password not configured — this feature stays inactive. Set it on the Settings page.
fp.auth.desc: For unlock and authorization, up to 5 (slots 0-4).
fp.switch.desc: Dedicated to switching between two hosts (slot 5); not used for unlock. Once enrolled, press this fingerprint on the device to switch to the other host.

inject.capture.failed: Capture failed — didn't land on a valid control (or landed on this locator). Try again, dropping right on the password box.
inject.capture.hint: Drag the crosshair onto the target app's password box and release. Keep the target window visible and not covered by this window.

inject.presets.desc: Known apps ship with immurok — add one and you only need to enter your own password. The app identity is pinned by package family name and code signature, so it survives app updates.
inject.subtitle: Locate a target app's password box and bind a dedicated password. On a fingerprint touch it is filled into the matching app.
inject.title: Custom
inject.warn.notpassword: Heads up: the located element isn't a password box.
inject.warn.pathonly: Note: this app is neither packaged nor signed, so it can only be matched by its executable path. The match breaks if the app moves or updates into a versioned folder, and a path is not proof of identity.

The device is not connected, so pairing cannot start.

Pair and connect the immurok device in Windows Bluetooth settings first. If it is currently linked to the other host, disconnect it there (or move that host out of range), then try again.

msg.unbind.local_only_confirm: The bound device is not connected, so it cannot be notified. This will clear the local binding only — the slot on that device stays occupied until you clear it there. You can then pair with a new device. Continue?
msg.unbind.local_only_hint: The bound device is not connected. Unbinding will clear the local binding only; its slot on the device stays occupied until you clear it there.
msg.unbind.local_only_ok: Local binding cleared. You can now pair with a new device.
msg.unbind.other_fail: Unbind failed (fingerprint rejected or timed out): {0}
msg.unbind.other_ok: The other host has been unbound.
msg.unbind.other_progress: Unbinding the other host (slot {0})… touch an enrolled fingerprint on the device to confirm.
msg.unbind.rejected: The device rejected the unbind: this host is not its active slot.
msg.unbind.rejected_offer: The device rejected the unbind — this host is not its active slot. This usually means the local binding belongs to a different device than the one now connected, so that binding is unusable. Clear the local binding anyway so you can pair with a new device?
msg.unbind.self_confirm: Unbinding this host clears its pairing slot on the device and the device will restart. You will need to pair again afterwards. Continue?
msg.unbind.self_ok: Unbound this PC; the device is restarting. It also erased its Bluetooth bond and will use a new address — remove the old immurok device in Windows Bluetooth settings and pair it again before reconnecting.
msg.unbind.self_progress: Unbinding this host… the device will restart.

setup.autostart.desc: Launch immurok automatically when you sign in. Password injection runs inside this app, so if it is not running, autofill silently does nothing.
setup.autostart.fail: Could not write the registry entry; auto-start is unchanged.
setup.cp.desc: After installation, the lock screen shows the immurok fingerprint-unlock tile. Importing the registry requires administrator rights (done by the installer).
setup.pass.desc: Submitted to the system on unlock. Stored in Windows Credential Manager, never sent over BLE.
setup.pass.hint: A Microsoft account sign-in name may differ from the local username; if unlock fails, re-save the password here using your sign-in email.
setup.pass.label: Login password
setup.ssh.desc: When enabled, ssh / git sign with the device's SSH private key (each signature needs a fingerprint touch).
setup.ssh.note: Turning this on stops the built-in Windows ssh-agent and points git at the native OpenSSH; turning it off puts both back.
